transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-20 16:00 UTC
Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees: Maya, Daniel (Redwood); Zoe, Rajiv, Elena (Pegasus Labs)

Summary: quick PLG/self-serve discovery for Redwood hosted API with notes on Dedicated/Private options. Customer interested in free credits, time-to-first-token, latency/cost tradeoffs and security (SOC2, SSO, VPC/KMS).

00:00 Zoe Martinez: hey everyone, thanks for doing this. we wanted a quick call to see how fast we can get up and running with Redwood, and whether hosted makes sense vs, you know, dedicated or private for our use case.
00:18 Maya (Redwood AE): thanks Zoe, yeah great to meet you all. I'm Maya, i'm the AE on this account, and daniel is our solutions engineer. we're focused on quickstart flow — free credits, SDKs, time-to-first-token. can you give a quick run-down of your current stack and what you're trying to build?
00:33 Zoe: sure, i'm zoe, cto. Pegasus builds an internal assistant for our R&D teams, plus a customer-facing summarization feature. we have privacy regs so some workloads need to stay in-region. currently using Anthropic for some prototyping, and a small self-hosted inference cluster for sensitive data.
00:50 Rajiv: hi i'm rajiv, ml eng. main constraints: low latency for the internal assistant (~150ms p95 preferred), cost that scales, and ability to pin model versions for reproducible outputs. also concerned about KV cache behavior with long convo context.
01:08 Daniel (Redwood SE): great context. for PLG/self-serve our hosted API gives fastest time-to-first-token — you can sign up, get API key, and use SDKs. we also give free credits for evaluation. typical quickstart for devs is < 30 minutes to first call if you have a simple prompt.
01:26 Elena: do you have an example deck or quickstart we can share internally?
01:29 Maya: yes i'll share the Quickstart.pdf and a one-click repo. also we'll include the free credits activation link.
01:37 Zoe: how does dedicated differ? like we want predictable throughput for certain times, but maybe keep low-volume stuff on hosted.
01:44 Daniel: Dedicated is reserved capacity — think of it as a private pool of GPUs for your org. it gives predictable throughput and priority scheduling, so if you need consistent 150ms p95 under load, Dedicated or a hybrid approach is common. Hosted is multi-tenant but we tune for low latency; your p95 depends on model choice and config.
02:05 Rajiv: what about private/VPC? we have some datasets that cannot leave our VPC due to compliance.
02:10 Daniel: private offering puts the control plane in your VPC or on-prem. we support KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs. for strict data residency you'd look at Private deployment. there is an onboarding effort and infra responsibility so timeline is longer than hosted.
02:26 Zoe: got it. can you ballpark time to production for each?
02:30 Maya: Hosted — minutes to hours for a demo/proof-of-concept. Dedicated — weeks to provision and configure, especially if you need reserved capacity. Private — months for on-prem/air-gapped setups, depending on procurement.
02:44 Rajiv: okay, on latency: you mentioned model choice matters. which models do you host and how are they tuned for latency vs cost?
02:52 Daniel: we have a catalog of open models and Redwood-verified profiles. you can choose smaller LLaMA variants for low latency, or larger ones for quality. we also offer quantized builds and recommend kernel selection; the runtime does compilation and kernel selection based on seq length. caching (prefix/KV) helps for chat-heavy flows to reduce tokens and latency.
03:15 Zoe: any gotchas with streaming or tool-calls?
03:19 Daniel: streaming is supported in hosted SDKs. functions/tool-calls are supported too; if you plan heavy tool usage, we recommend testing with our streaming endpoints to measure latency.
03:30 Elena: security — do you have SOC 2 and SSO integrations? we use Okta.
03:35 Maya: yes SOC 2 Type II, SAML/SSO via Okta, RBAC, and per-token auditing in the Console. i'll attach our security overview link in the follow-up.
03:47 Zoe: good. also interested in data retention policies and purge.
03:51 Daniel: we support configurable retention and customer-managed KMS for Private. Hosted has retention defaults but enterprise customers can opt-in for shorter retention or dedicated retention policies; i'll share details.
04:05 Rajiv: one of our concerns is cold-start latency for long sequences, and how KV cache persists across requests. is that something Redwood's runtime handles?
04:13 Daniel: yes, runtime keeps a KV cache to avoid re-computing prefixes. caching behavior depends on sticky routing and session affinity — Dedicated makes it easier to keep warm cache. hosted does cache but with multi-tenant routing could be more eviction. for POC we can simulate your traffic patterns to show p95 improvements.
04:36 Zoe: sounds good. what's the instrumentation? how do we debug slow requests?
04:40 Daniel: Console has per-route latency, token-level cost breakdown, traces and request IDs. you can export traces to jaeger or our tracing hooks.
04:50 Elena: what's the pricing model for hosted — per-token + embeddings?
04:54 Maya: yes hosted is usage-based: per-token generation and per-embedding unit. we'll send a pricing sheet; Dedicated is reserved monthly/annual. we also have add-ons for extended observability retention and premium SLA.
05:08 Rajiv: can we run some benchmarks — p95 latency and cost per 1k requests — before committing?
05:12 Daniel: absolutely. next step: you share sample payloads and sequence lengths, and we'll run a benchmark on hosted sandbox or a small Dedicated sim. we'll share a benchmark spreadsheet.
05:24 Zoe: timeline — we want a POC by early march, ideally with a small cohort of users. is that realistic?
05:30 Maya: yes that's doable with hosted quickstart + credits. if you later need Dedicated we can kick off provisioning in parallel.
05:36 Rajiv: are there any vendor lock-in concerns with your SDKs?
05:39 Daniel: our APIs are standard REST and SDKs are lightweight. you can run calls to hosted or to dedicated/private endpoints; rollouts let you pin versions. exportability varies if you use Private on-prem.
05:52 Elena: any competitors we should consider?
05:54 Maya: folks commonly evaluate OpenAI and Anthropic for hosted, and AWS Bedrock for deeper cloud integration. we see teams choose based on latency, cost, compliance needs.
06:04 Zoe: ok can we see a quick demo of creating an API key and doing the first call?
06:08 Maya: we can walk through the quick steps now, but i'll also send a one-click quickstart repo.
06:12 Daniel: (screen share) step 1: create account, enable free credits, get API key. step 2: install redwood sdk pip install redwood-client (note: transcript may mis-type package name). example call: client.generate(prompt...). you'll see streaming and full response.
06:33 Rajiv: any rate limits on free credits environment?
06:36 Maya: yes we throttle sandbox to protect multitenant capacity; we'll note limits in the quickstart. for dedicated you can set higher throughput.
06:45 Zoe: on the security docs — will you share SOC2 report and pen-test summary?
06:49 Maya: yes, i'll include SOC2 summary and our pen test executive summary link; for full reports we do an NDA/EA.
06:58 Rajiv: for benchmarking, what's the recommended metric set? p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens per request, cold vs warm, cost per 1k tokens?
07:06 Daniel: exactly. also measure concurrency and tail latency under your expected traffic. we'll provide a sample script that sends traffic with your token distribution.
07:18 Zoe: okay next steps then?
07:21 Maya: recap: 1) Maya to send Quickstart, security docs, pricing and free credits link. 2) Rajiv to share sample payloads and traffic distribution. 3) Daniel will run a hosted sandbox benchmark and return results + spreadsheet. 4) Zoe to confirm POC timeline internal stakeholders by 2026-03-10.
07:42 Elena: who should we loop in for procurement if we need dedicated?
07:45 Maya: i'll include our sales ops contact in the follow-up. Dedicated provisioning requires comms with Sales Ops and Solutions Engineering.
07:54 Zoe: great, thanks everyone.
07:56 Maya: thanks all — we'll follow up with links and action items.

Notes/Artifacts mentioned: Quickstart.pdf (link), Security-Overview.pdf (link), Benchmark-template.xlsx (link)

End of transcript.
